official.application_route: Online application via the My Visegrad system (my.visegradfund.org) during the call window; the host institution receives a separate per-semester contribution.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizenship or residence in Czechia, Hungary, Poland or Slovakia, or in an EaP/WB country; the host institution must be in a different country from the applicant's citizenship.
official.international_eligibility: Designed for cross-border mobility: Visegrad country nationals study in another Visegrad or EaP/WB country, and EaP/WB nationals study in Visegrad countries.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All disciplines; master's and post-master's levels at accredited institutions in the participating countries.
official.research_requirement: Post-Master's level applicants need a scanned letter of acceptance with a detailed working plan.
official.duration: 1-2 semesters of full-time master's-level study or full-time post-master's (doctoral, postdoctoral) study or research
official.description: The Visegrad Scholarship Program supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for up to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe, funded by the International Visegrad Fund.

applicant_utility.summary: The Visegrad Scholarship pays EUR 3,500 per semester directly to the scholar, plus EUR 2,000 per semester to the host institution, for one or two semesters of full-time master's or post-master's study or research across more than 190 institutions in Central and Eastern Europe. The eligibility geography is the part applicants underestimate: your host country must differ from your citizenship country, your previous studies must have been completed in yet another country, and the host must sit more than 150 km from your current university or permanent residence. The call opens 1 January 2027 and shuts hard at noon on 15 April 2027, with results at the end of May, so mobility realistically starts in September or October.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's, doctoral and postdoctoral students and researchers from the Visegrad Four or EaP/WB countries planning a 1-2 semester exchange with a V4-relevant topic.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify the host institution's country differs from your citizenship country and that your previous studies were completed elsewhere
Measure the distance between your permanent residence or current university and the host: it must exceed 150 km
If not yet accepted at application, secure a letter of acceptance from the host university or documented proof of applying
For post-master's level, arrange the letter of acceptance with a detailed working plan
Prepare certified translations early - sworn-translator or university-official certification is required for non-English documents
Diarise the 15 April 12:00 PM (noon) cut-off; the My Visegrad system will not wait
common_rejection_risks: Host institution in the same country as your citizenship, which is an automatic fail
Previous university studies completed in the country of application
The 150 km distance rule disqualifying a host close to home
Uploading documents separately or after the deadline instead of one complete submission
Applying as a previously supported scholar without a strong justification, since preference favours first-time applicants
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and fees beyond what the host institution's EUR 2,000 per semester covers, plus any travel, insurance and living costs beyond the EUR 3,500 per-semester stipend.
document_audit: Master's applicants need transcripts covering at least the last two completed semesters or a diploma supplement
Post-master's applicants need the acceptance letter bundled with a detailed working plan - a bare acceptance letter is not enough
Translations must be certified by a sworn translator or a university official; informal translations fail
Your topic's relevance to the V4 region is a stated selection preference, so make it explicit in the application
alerts: Results come at the end of May, so a funded stay cannot begin before September/October - plan any academic-year commitments around that
The 2027/28 call only opens on 1 January 2027 at 12:00 PM; earlier submissions are impossible
Separate Visegrad instruments (Visegrad Fellowship, Visegrad Postdoc, Visegrad-Taiwan Scholarships) run on their own calendars and are not covered by this application
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Assemble ID, transcripts and the host acceptance (or proof of applying) with certified translations, submit everything in one upload through My Visegrad before noon on 15 April, and await the end-of-May results.

official.deadline_note: The 2027 cycle runs two windows: Application Window #1 from January 18 to February 26, 2027 and Application Window #2 from March 29 to May 21, 2027. The link to the JJ/WBGSP application form is only communicated to candidates admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to a participating master's programme and shortlisted as eligible by that university, and each participating university sets its own admission deadlines, which fall before the JJ/WBGSP window closes.
official.application_cycle: 2027 cycle; Application Window #1 January 18 - February 26, 2027 and Application Window #2 March 29 - May 21, 2027, timed to match participating programmes' academic calendars.
official.status_note: The World Bank has announced the dates of the 2027 application windows for developing country nationals and published the updated list of JJ/WBGSP eligible countries.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The World Bank states the scholarship provides tuition for the graduate programme and the cost of basic medical insurance obtained through the university.
benefits: Tuition for the graduate programme and the cost of basic medical insurance obtained through the university
Monthly subsistence allowance covering all living expenses while on campus (accommodation, food, books); the amount varies by host country
Economy-class air travel between the home country and the host university at the start of the programme and immediately after the scholarship period
Travel allowance of US$600 for each trip
Participation in the JJ/WBGSP alumni community of more than 7,000 mid-career professionals from 160 developing countries and Japan
eligibility: National of a World Bank member developing country on the published 2027 eligible list; not holding dual citizenship of any developed country
Bachelor's (or equivalent) degree earned at least 3 years prior to the application deadline date

Employed in development-related work in a paid full-time position at the time of submitting the application, with at least 3 years of paid development-related employment since earning the bachelor's degree, acquired within the past 6 years from the application deadline date

On or before the deadline, admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to at least one JJ/WBGSP participating master's programme located outside the applicant's country of citizenship and residence; the admission letter must be uploaded before submitting the application
Not an Executive Director, alternate or staff member of any type of appointment of the World Bank Group, nor a close relative by blood or adoption of any of them
Not previously offered a JJ/WBGSP scholarship and declined it, and not previously received one without graduating
requirements: Hold an unconditional admission letter (except for funding) from a JJ/WBGSP participating master's programme outside the country of citizenship and residence, uploaded before submitting the application
The link to the JJ/WBGSP application form is communicated only to candidates admitted unconditionally and shortlisted as eligible by the participating university
All eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to with no exceptions and do not change during an open call
If awarded another scholarship or fellowship, send the documents to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat, since the scholarship may only supplement and not duplicate other support
Commit to return to the home country after earning the degree
documents: Letter of admission from a JJ/WBGSP participating master's programme, uploaded before submitting the application
JJ/WBGSP application form, accessed through the link communicated only to shortlisted candidates
Professional recommendations evaluated as part of the application
Documents pertaining to any other scholarship or fellowship held, sent to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat
selection_criteria: Two qualified assessors independently score each eligible application from 1 to 10 on four factors: quality of professional experience (30%), quality of professional recommendations (30%), quality of commitment to the home country (30%), and quality of education background (10%)

The Secretariat uses the average score plus wide geographical distribution, reasonable gender distribution, unusual circumstances or hardships, and preference for applicants with limited access to financial resources
Finalists are presented to the JJ/WBGSP Steering Committee, composed of World Bank Board of Directors members and World Bank management, for approval
coverage: Tuition and basic medical insurance obtained through the university
Monthly subsistence allowance for all living expenses on campus, varying by host country
Economy-class air travel plus a US$600 travel allowance for each trip

The scholarship does not cover visa application costs, family expenses, extra-curricular courses or training, sub-minimum-credit courses, language training outside the graduate programme, additional travel during study, research or supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships, educational equipment such as computers, or the resident permit fee
application_method: Choose a target from the published list of participating master's programmes for the relevant window
Apply directly to that university and satisfy its own admission requirements and internal deadlines
Be admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to the participating programme
Ask the university whether you meet both conditions - unconditional admission and shortlisting as an eligible JJ/WBGSP applicant
Once shortlisted, the university communicates the link to the JJ/WBGSP application form
Upload the admission letter and submit the application within the window (January 18 - February 26 or March 29 - May 21, 2027)
official.application_route: First win unconditional admission to one of the 44 participating master's programmes; the university then shortlists you and issues the link to the JJ/WBGSP application form.
official.citizenship_residency: Nationals of World Bank member developing countries on the published 2027 eligible list, without dual citizenship of any developed country; the host programme must be outside the country of citizenship and residence.
official.international_eligibility: For developing-country nationals studying outside their home country at a participating university.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Development-related topics only, at one of 44 participating master's programmes in 24 universities in the U.S., Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan; admission to a non-participating programme makes you ineligible.
official.duration: The duration of the graduate programme or two years, whichever is less
official.description: The Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program is available to citizens of certain developing countries with relevant professional experience who are applying to a master's degree programme in a development-related topic. Funded solely by the Government of Japan on an annual basis, it provides tuition, a monthly living stipend, round-trip airfare, health insurance and a travel allowance.

not_confirmed: Monthly subsistence allowance amount (the World Bank states it varies by host country and is not published)
English language requirement (no programme-level requirement is published; participating universities set their own admission language rules)
verification.notes: The World Bank's official JJ/WBGSP page was fetched on 2026-10-10: the 2027 window dates (January 18 - February 26 and March 29 - May 21, 2027), the full benefits list including the US$600 travel allowance per trip, the eligibility criteria, the two-assessor scoring weights and the non-covered items list were read directly from the page.

applicant_utility.summary: JJ/WBGSP is a full package for mid-career development professionals: tuition, basic medical insurance, a monthly living stipend whose size the World Bank does not publish, economy flights and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip, at one of only 44 participating master's programmes. The scholarship is strictly second in line to admission - you must first hold an unconditional (except funding) offer from a participating programme outside your home country, and only then does the university hand you the application link. Scoring weights your development track record heavily: professional experience, recommendations and commitment to your home country are 30% each, so a strong CV matters more than academic pedigree.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career development professionals from listed developing countries with a bachelor's earned at least three years before the deadline and three years of relevant paid work inside the past six years.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your country is on the World Bank's published 2027 eligible countries list before anything else
Pick a target from the 44 participating master's programmes and apply through that university's own admission process, respecting its internal deadlines
Secure unconditional admission (except for funding) before the JJ/WBGSP window closes, since the admission letter must be uploaded with the application
Ask the participating university directly whether it will shortlist you for the JJ/WBGSP application link
Prepare referees who can speak to your development experience, commitment to your home country and education background
If you hold another scholarship or fellowship, ready those documents for the Secretariat
common_rejection_risks: Admission to a non-participating programme, which makes you ineligible for 2027
Host programme located inside your country of citizenship or residence
Less than three years of paid development-related employment, or experience acquired outside the past six years
Declining an earlier JJ/WBGSP offer, or having received one without graduating - both bar reapplication permanently
World Bank staff, Executive Directors' alternates or their close relatives applying
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa application costs, expenses to bring or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, sub-minimum-credit courses, language training outside the programme, additional travel during study, research or supplementary materials, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships, computers, and the resident permit fee.
document_audit: The admission letter must be unconditional except for funding; conditional offers do not satisfy the rule
The application form link arrives only via the participating university - there is no public standalone form
Two independent assessors score the file, so make the experience, recommendations and home-country commitment sections mutually consistent
Evidence of any other scholarship must go to the Secretariat, since the award only supplements and never duplicates other support
alerts: Eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to with no exceptions and do not change during an open call
Applicants from Fragile and Conflict States listed in Annex 3 of the Application Guidelines may have limited employment opportunities taken into account
Scholars commit to returning to their home country after earning the degree
University admission deadlines fall before the JJ/WBGSP window closes, so start the admission process months ahead of January or March
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Win unconditional admission at a participating programme, ask that university to shortlist you, use the application-form link it provides to submit with your admission letter inside the window, then await Steering Committee approval.
